query: How does resolution time vary across category, priority, and assignment group?

per_column.name: infrastructure_domain
per_column.rationale: Categorizes incidents by technical domain (VPN, network, database, email), giving a genuine new grouping axis that complements the existing 'category' column and is directly useful for comparing resolution time. Values are sound readings of short_description across all samples.

per_column.name: problem_severity
per_column.rationale: Severity is a useful axis for explaining resolution-time variation. However, values are somewhat inferential: 'connectivity_blocking' vs 'partial_access' for terse descriptions like 'VPN connection issue' or 'Email system not working properly' involves guesswork not fully warranted by the text, though generally plausible.

per_column.name: resolution_completion_status
per_column.rationale: This boolean is largely redundant with the existing 'state'/'closed_at' fields (a closed record is complete), so it adds little new analytical leverage for resolution-time comparison. Values are derivable from closed_at presence.

per_column.name: incident_scope
per_column.rationale: Scope (single user vs department vs system-wide) is a genuinely useful axis for explaining resolution time. Groundedness is mixed: 'WiFi in sales department' correctly maps to department-scoped, but 'Email system not working properly' -> 'system_wide_service' and 'VPN connection issue' -> 'single_user_affected' are inferences the terse text does not clearly support.

per_column.name: authentication_access_failure
per_column.rationale: A binary access-failure flag offers a modest additional cross-tab axis. Values in samples (all False for connectivity/email issues) are reasonable readings, though it is a fairly generic single-flag feature.

per_column.name: technician_assignment_continuity
per_column.rationale: Assignment continuity could relate to resolution time, but the value is not derivable from the sampled source text (short_description/timestamps); it would require assigned_to vs closed_by comparison not shown. The True/False assignments in samples appear unsupported by provided evidence.

judge.rationale: Several columns (infrastructure_domain, problem_severity, incident_scope) provide genuine new grouping axes well-aligned with the query about resolution-time variation, and are largely grounded in short_description. resolution_completion_status is largely redundant with existing state/closed fields. Groundedness is weakened by inferential severity/scope labels on terse text and by technician_assignment_continuity, whose values are not derivable from the sampled evidence.
